name: Convex-Geometry Ideals Are Conditional Antimatroids
scope: Finite one-inclusion graphs, up to signed-coordinate equivalence and suppression of constants.
statement: Every lower ideal of a finite convex geometry is a bouquet of convex geometries and hence a conditional antimatroid.
proof: The ideal contains the empty set and inherits intersection closure from the ambient convex geometry. If $Y\subsetneq X$ belong to the ideal, the ambient convex-geometry extension axiom supplies a one-element extension of $Y$ inside $X$; downward closure keeps that extension in the ideal.
comments: CCK Proposition 4 proves strictness for oriented set families. This record does not strengthen that example to a signed-coordinate graph-class separation.
